edge.title: The estimate that grows
edge.setup: An admission with a quoted package. By discharge the bill has grown — consumables, a consultant visit you don't remember, a room upgrade 'because nothing else was free'. Insurance covers part; the cash difference is yours, and you're being asked to settle before discharge while someone is still in a bed.
edge.tell: You're being asked to agree to money at the exact moment you are least able to walk away.
move: Ask for the itemised bill, not the summary — and ask on day one, not at discharge. Daily interim bills are your right and they stop surprises compounding.
Get the insurer's pre-authorisation in writing before a planned procedure, with the package explicitly named.
Question room-category upgrades: most policies cap room rent, and exceeding it can proportionally cut your entire claim, not just the room charge.
Unresolved: the hospital's grievance cell, then the insurance ombudsman — free, and genuinely effective on billing disputes.
edge.why: The leverage asymmetry is total — the other party controls information, time and someone you love. The only workable counter is to move every decision earlier, to a moment when you can still ask questions. Pre-authorisation and daily bills are both just ways of buying back time.
edge.variants: Same shape: mechanics calling mid-repair, vets at the consultation, any quote where work has already begun.

lens.name: The availability heuristic
lens.one_line: You judge how likely something is by how easily an example comes to mind.
lens.detail: Ease of recall is driven by how recent, vivid and emotionally charged an event was — not its frequency. News selects for exactly those properties, so consuming more news systematically distorts your risk sense rather than sharpening it. This is the single strongest argument for reading less news and understanding more structure.
elsewhere: Fearing a kidnapping while texting at the wheel.
Overrating lottery odds after a winner is interviewed.
Believing an industry is collapsing because layoffs are covered and hiring isn't.
lens.test: Am I estimating this from data, or from how easily a story came to mind?
lens.today: Three outlets ran the Jaguar-into-a-petrol-bunk fire near Attibele on the same day, so it will be the first thing you recall when you next pull up at a pump. The thing that actually costs you daily is quieter: Moneycontrol reports that on a ₹12 lakh salary, Bengaluru traffic can cost nearly ₹1 lakh a year in lost time. The vivid event gets the headlines; the dull recurring one gets your money.

moved.what: A 20-day traffic diversion has begun on Basavanagar Road, per Urban Acres.
moved.so_what: If Basavanagar Road is on your route, try an alternative before a day that matters. The reports I fetched give no diversion details, so check the Traffic Police advisory.

moved.what: The Blue Line airport corridor (58 km, Central Silk Board to KIA) is reported delayed to March 2028 and will open in phases. Separately, CMRS has finished its safety inspection of the Pink Line's elevated section.
moved.so_what: Do not choose a flat or a job on the assumption of a metro to the airport before 2028. For the Pink Line, wait for BMRCL's opening date before changing your commute.

moved.what: BMTC is reported to be sharing real-time bus data with Namma Yatri, BIAL and Tummoc.
moved.so_what: If you take buses, check whether live arrival times now show in the app you already use before you add another one. The report gives no launch date.

moved.what: The GST Council has unveiled reforms that ease penalties and speed up refunds, per Business Standard.
moved.so_what: If you file GST as a freelancer or small business, ask your accountant what changes for late-filing penalties and refund timelines. For ordinary shopping, nothing changes on your bill today.

moved.what: Karnataka's food regulator FDA found expired ingredients at two ice cream units in Bengaluru.
moved.so_what: Buy ice cream from sealed, branded packs and check the manufacturing and expiry dates. Treat loose, unbranded scoops from unfamiliar vendors with caution.

carry_over.prompt: A stranger offers gold well below market and says it must stay quiet and be bought quickly. What is the tell?
carry_over.answer: A price below market, with a story that explains why it must be quick and secret.
